newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU says vets Spanish soccer TV rights deal.
newsitem.headline: EU says vets Spanish soccer TV rights deal.

text.p: Spanish digital television company CanalSatelite and its partners have asked the European Commission to clear an agreement to exploit the broadcasting rights to the Spanish soccer league and cup, the Commission said on Monday.
The rights concern the seasons 1998/99 to 2002/2003, it said in notice published in the EU's Official Journal.

They were BOUGHT by a subsidiary of Sogecable, itself a joint venture between Canal Plus and Promotora de Informaciones SA, commercial television channel Antena 3 and Televio de Catalunya and subsequently pooled in a joint venture called Audiovisual Sport SL.
CanalSatelite is Spain's first digital pay-TV and pay-per-view channel, which is 85 percent owned by Sogecable and 15 percent by Antena 3. Its pay-per-view channel begun broadcasting last month.

Under the terms of the notified agreement, CanalSatelite has exclusive pay-per-view rights for the championships at stake, the remaining rights being distributed between Sogecable, Antena 3 and the catalan station, the Commission's notice said.
It added that CanalSatelite would carry out the subscribers management activities.
The Commission said the deal could fall under Regulation 17/62, which bans agreements or concerted practices which harm fair competition and abuse of a dominant position.
Although there is no deadline to rule on agreements falling under such rules the Commission did ask interested parties to submit their comments within 20 days.
The launch of digital television in Spain has been the centre of a huge controversy setting CanalSatelite against a rival project led by recently privatised telecommunications firm Telefonica.

The Spanish government is reported to be concerned by CanalSatelite's acquisition of exclusive rights to the country's soccer league games, prefering instead that such popular sports events continue to be viewed by a wider audience.
